subject: religious liberty, nonpreference, establishment, witness and juror eligibility
legal_effect: Protects free exercise and enjoyment of religion without discrimination or preference, bars legislative establishment of religion, and bars religious belief from making a person incompetent as a witness or juror.
religion_connection: Directly limits state religious preference and protects religious exercise and civic participation regardless of religious belief.
scope_note: Historical motive is not assigned in the current verified profile.
notes: Normalized from the verified California baseline.

subject: sectarian schools, public funding, and public-school instruction
legal_effect: Bars public money for sectarian or denominational schools or schools outside public-school control and bars sectarian or denominational doctrine in the common schools.
religion_connection: Restricts state support for sectarian institutions and sectarian doctrine in public schools.
scope_note: Application is subject to controlling federal constitutional doctrine concerning neutral public-benefit programs; historical motive is not assigned in this pass.
notes: Normalized from the verified California baseline.

subject: public aid to religious entities
legal_effect: Restricts specified appropriations, grants, public funds, and donations in aid of religious sects, churches, creeds, sectarian purposes, and institutions controlled by religious bodies, subject to stated exceptions.
religion_connection: Directly limits specified forms of public financial support for religious organizations and sectarian purposes.
scope_note: Application is constrained by federal constitutional doctrine where applicable; historical motive is not assigned in this pass.
notes: Normalized from the verified California baseline.

subject: religious accommodation in employment
legal_effect: Requires covered employers or entities to reasonably accommodate conflicts between employment requirements and religious belief or observance unless accommodation cannot be made without undue hardship.
religion_connection: Protects religious belief and observance from specified employment burdens and expressly addresses holy-day observance, religious dress, and grooming practices.
scope_note: Coverage and exceptions depend on the statutory definitions and limits in the Fair Employment and Housing Act.
notes: Normalized from the verified California baseline.

subject: worship, conscience, nonpreference, compelled support, and religious tests
legal_effect: Protects worship according to conscience, limits interference with religious opinion and conscience, bars legal preference for a creed or mode of worship, bars compelled support of worship or ministry, and bars religious tests for offices of trust or profit.
religion_connection: Directly limits state religious preference, coercion, and religious qualification while protecting religious conscience.
scope_note: This record groups closely related constitutional provisions for the first-pass baseline.
primary_authority: Indiana Constitution, Article I, §§ 2–5, via Indiana State Library — https://www.in.gov/library/collections-and-services/indiana/subject-guides-to-indiana-collection-materials/indiana-constitution/
notes: Normalized from the verified Indiana baseline.

subject: treasury aid to religious or theological institutions
legal_effect: States that no money shall be drawn from the treasury for the benefit of a religious or theological institution.
religion_connection: Restricts direct treasury support for religious or theological institutions.
scope_note: Not an absolute ban on every neutral public-benefit program involving religious schools; Meredith v. Pence is part of the operative state-law context.
primary_authority: Indiana Constitution, Article I, § 6, via Indiana State Library — https://www.in.gov/library/collections-and-services/indiana/subject-guides-to-indiana-collection-materials/indiana-constitution/
notes: Historical-causation analysis remains separate.

subject: religious tests and Supreme Being proviso for public office
legal_effect: Bars religious tests for office or public trust but retains printed language allowing a qualification that a person acknowledge the existence of a Supreme Being.
religion_connection: The printed constitutional text contains an explicit religious-belief qualification.
scope_note: The explicit qualification remains printed but cannot operate consistently with controlling federal no-religious-test doctrine.
enforcement_note: The Supreme-Being qualification is incompatible with Torcaso v. Watkins, 367 U.S. 488 (1961).
notes: Classification A describes the printed religious qualification; operative federal doctrine separately limits enforcement.

subject: nonsectarian condition in school tuition assistance
legal_effect: Formerly imposed a nonsectarian condition relevant to school eligibility for Maine's tuition-assistance framework; the subsection has been repealed.
religion_connection: The former condition restricted eligibility based on sectarian or religious status and became subject to federal Free Exercise constraints.
scope_note: Carson v. Makin addressed the exclusion of schools providing religious instruction from the tuition-assistance program at issue. The current official § 2951 page shows subsection 2 repealed.
notes: Normalized from the verified Maine baseline.

subject: public aid for sectarian purposes and religiously controlled institutions
legal_effect: Prohibits specified public appropriations or payments for sectarian purposes or to institutions controlled by a church, sect, or denomination.
religion_connection: Restricts specified public support for sectarian purposes and religiously controlled institutions.
scope_note: The constitutional text remains, but Espinoza limits application that excludes otherwise eligible religious schools from the scholarship program at issue solely because of religious status.
primary_authority: Montana Constitution art. X, § 6, official Legislature publication
explanatory_authority: Espinoza v. Montana Department of Revenue, 591 U.S. 464 (2020)
notes: Historical origins require separate research before assigning causal labels.

subject: religious liberty, religious tests, church-state union, and public support
legal_effect: Protects conscience and free exercise, bars establishment and religious tests for office and voting, protects witness and juror eligibility regardless of belief, bars union of church and state, and restricts public support for religious worship or establishments.
religion_connection: Directly limits state religious coercion, qualification, establishment, and public support while protecting religious liberty.
scope_note: Historical causation remains pending and is not inferred from the present text.
notes: Normalized from the verified Utah baseline.

subject: religious tests in education and direct public support for religiously controlled schools
legal_effect: Bars religious or partisan tests in the state's education systems and bars state and local appropriations for direct support of schools or educational institutions controlled by religious organizations.
religion_connection: Limits religious qualification in education and direct public financial support for religiously controlled educational institutions.
scope_note: This first-pass record groups the related Article X education clauses.
notes: Historical-causation analysis remains pending.

subject: free exercise and substantial government burdens
legal_effect: Provides a statutory free-exercise standard under which government may not substantially burden a person's free exercise unless the burden satisfies a compelling-interest and least-restrictive-means standard, with specified claims, defenses, and remedies.
religion_connection: Protects religious exercise against specified governmental burdens.
scope_note: Current cited text effective July 1, 2025.
notes: Normalized from the verified Utah baseline.

formal_citation: Utah Code § 53G-10-202, as amended by 2026 S.B. 268
subject: religion in public-school curriculum, prayer, devotionals, and student expression
legal_effect: Permits academically framed study of religion and its influence, bars public-school sponsorship or denial of prayer or religious devotionals, bars officials from endorsing or disparaging religious or nonreligious viewpoints, and protects students from discrimination based on religious perspectives in assignments.
religion_connection: Regulates government treatment of religion in public schools through viewpoint-neutrality, nonendorsement, and student-expression protections.
scope_note: This D classification addresses the neutrality and student-expression provisions described in the verified profile.
notes: Classification does not establish legislative motive.

formal_citation: Utah Code § 53G-10-302, as amended by 2026 S.B. 268
subject: religion and religious materials in public-school American history instruction
legal_effect: Expressly includes the role of religion and religious liberty in American-history instruction, includes the Ten Commandments in the statutory historical-document list, and requires display of the national motto in public-school buildings.
religion_connection: The enacted legal text expressly references religion, religious liberty, and the Ten Commandments.
scope_note: Classification A records explicit religion-linked content; it does not by itself establish a religious historical cause for enactment.
notes: Historical causation remains a separate research question.

subject: conscience, nonpreference, religious tests, and juror qualifications
legal_effect: Protects worship according to conscience, bars compelled support and legal preference for religious establishment or worship, bars religious tests for public office or trust beyond the constitutional oath, and bars religious tests for jurors.
religion_connection: Directly limits state religious preference, compelled support, and religious qualification for public service.
scope_note: This first-pass record groups related Tennessee Bill of Rights provisions.
primary_authority: Tennessee Secretary of State, 2023 Constitution of Tennessee — https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/pub/2023%20TN%20Constitution.pdf
notes: Normalized from the verified Tennessee baseline.

subject: clergy disqualification from the legislature
legal_effect: The printed constitutional text declares ministers of the Gospel and priests of any denomination ineligible for seats in the Tennessee legislature.
religion_connection: Creates an explicit office disqualification based on clerical religious status.
scope_note: The provision remains printed but is unenforceable under controlling federal constitutional law.
enforcement_note: McDaniel v. Paty, 435 U.S. 618 (1978), held the clergy disqualification unconstitutional as applied through the qualification at issue.
primary_authority: Tennessee Secretary of State, 2023 Constitution of Tennessee — https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/pub/2023%20TN%20Constitution.pdf
notes: Text-on-books status is distinct from enforceability.

subject: belief-in-God qualification for civil office
legal_effect: The printed constitutional text disqualifies a person who denies the being of God or a future state of rewards and punishments from civil office.
religion_connection: Creates an explicit religious-belief qualification for civil office.
scope_note: The provision remains printed but cannot be enforced consistently with controlling federal no-religious-test doctrine.
enforcement_note: Torcaso v. Watkins, 367 U.S. 488 (1961), bars state religious-belief qualifications for public office.
primary_authority: Tennessee Secretary of State, 2023 Constitution of Tennessee — https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/pub/2023%20TN%20Constitution.pdf
notes: Text-on-books status is distinct from enforceability.

subject: statutory protection of religious exercise
legal_effect: Protects against government substantially burdening a person's free exercise of religion unless the burden satisfies an essential compelling-governmental-interest and least-restrictive-means standard, with specified claims, defenses, and remedies.
religion_connection: Protects religious exercise against specified governmental burdens.
scope_note: Originally enacted by Public Chapter 573 of 2009 and later amended; broader amendment history remains an expansion item.
notes: Normalized from the verified Tennessee baseline.

subject: freedom of conscience, religious qualifications, witnesses, and jurors
legal_effect: Protects freedom of conscience in religious matters, bars disturbance because of religion, bars religious qualifications for public office or employment, and protects witness and juror eligibility regardless of religious opinion.
religion_connection: Limits state religious coercion and qualification while protecting religious conscience and civic participation.
scope_note: The public-funding clause in the same section is normalized separately because its application is subject to distinct federal Free Exercise limits.
notes: Normalized from the verified Washington baseline.

subject: public money or property for religious worship, instruction, or establishment
legal_effect: Restricts public money or property from being appropriated for or applied to religious worship, exercise, instruction, or support of a religious establishment, subject to the constitutional text's exception and controlling federal doctrine.
religion_connection: Restricts specified public support for religious activity or establishment.
scope_note: The text remains in force, but application of state no-aid rules is constrained by federal Free Exercise doctrine; Locke v. Davey addressed the narrower ministerial-training context.
notes: Historical motive is not assigned in the current profile.

subject: sectarian control or influence in publicly supported schools
legal_effect: Requires schools maintained or supported wholly or partly by public funds to be free from sectarian control or influence.
religion_connection: Limits sectarian control or influence in publicly supported schools.
scope_note: Program-specific federal constitutional limits remain an expansion item.
notes: Historical causation remains separate.

subject: student religious expression in public schools
legal_effect: Protects public-school students' free-speech and free-exercise rights, permits relevant religious expression in assignments, and bars school personnel from imposing their own religious beliefs.
religion_connection: Protects private religious expression while limiting official religious coercion.
scope_note: Academic relevance and ordinary curricular requirements still apply.
notes: Normalized from the verified Washington baseline.

subject: faith or conscience excused school absences
legal_effect: Permits up to two excused school days per year for reasons of faith or conscience or organized activity under a religious organization, subject to statutory conditions including parental approval.
religion_connection: Creates an explicit faith-, conscience-, and religion-specific school attendance accommodation.
scope_note: Classification A describes the explicit religious category in the rule, not historical legislative motive.
notes: Normalized from the verified Washington baseline.

subject: health-care conscience and religious objections
legal_effect: Provides specified conscience protections for health carriers, facilities, and providers, including provisions addressing religiously sponsored entities and objections based on conscience or religion, while also regulating enrollee access and notice.
religion_connection: The statute expressly creates religion- and conscience-linked protections and obligations in health-care coverage and delivery.
scope_note: Application is fact-specific and depends on the statute's definitions and access requirements.
notes: Classification A does not establish a historical religious cause.

subject: religious freedom, compelled support, religious tests, and sect privileges
legal_effect: Protects religious profession and argument, bars compelled support of worship or ministry, bars burdens on civil capacities because of religious belief, bars religious tests and peculiar sect privileges, and bars specified compulsory taxation for worship or ministry.
religion_connection: Limits state religious coercion, qualification, preference, and compelled support while protecting religious liberty.
scope_note: Historical motive is not assigned in the first-pass profile.
explanatory_authority: West Virginia Religion & Law state profile
notes: Normalized from the verified West Virginia baseline.

subject: Equal Protection for Religion Act
legal_effect: Restricts state action that substantially burdens religious exercise absent a compelling governmental interest pursued by the least restrictive means and bars specified more-restrictive treatment of religious conduct than comparable nonreligious conduct.
religion_connection: Protects religious exercise from specified governmental burdens and unequal treatment.
scope_note: Claims, defenses, and remedies are governed by the Act's current text.
primary_authority: West Virginia Legislature, W. Va. Code ch. 35, art. 1A — https://code.wvlegislature.gov/35-1A/
explanatory_authority: West Virginia Religion & Law state profile
notes: Normalized from the verified West Virginia baseline.

subject: student religious expression and organizations
legal_effect: Protects students and parents against public-school discrimination based on religious viewpoint or expression and regulates voluntary religious expression, assignments, activities, organizations, and messages subject to academic and constitutional limits.
religion_connection: Protects private religious expression from school discrimination while preserving limits on compelled or official religious activity.
scope_note: The Act does not excuse students from otherwise valid academic requirements merely because a required answer conflicts with belief.
primary_authority: West Virginia Legislature, W. Va. Code ch. 18, art. 33 — https://code.wvlegislature.gov/18-33/
explanatory_authority: West Virginia Religion & Law state profile
notes: Normalized from the verified West Virginia baseline.

subject: elective public-school courses on the Bible
legal_effect: Permits elective high-school social-studies courses concerning the Hebrew Scriptures or Old Testament, the New Testament, or both, for academic study of literary, historical, and cultural influence under statutory religious-neutrality requirements.
religion_connection: The statute expressly authorizes courses centered on named religious scriptures and prescribes neutral treatment.
scope_note: Classification A records explicit religion-linked subject matter; it does not establish enactment motive.
primary_authority: West Virginia Legislature, W. Va. Code § 18-2-9a — https://code.wvlegislature.gov/18-2-9a/
explanatory_authority: West Virginia Religion & Law state profile
notes: Neutrality safeguards are part of the legal effect.

subject: religious liberty, conscience, nonpreference, and public support
legal_effect: Protects worship according to conscience, bars compelled attendance at or support of worship or ministry, bars interference with conscience and legal preference for religious establishments, and restricts treasury money for specified religious entities.
religion_connection: Limits state religious coercion, preference, and specified public support while protecting religious conscience.
scope_note: A proposed 2026 amendment concerning emergency closure of places of worship is pending voter ratification and is not part of this current-law record.
notes: Historical causation remains separate.

subject: sectarian instruction in district schools
legal_effect: Requires district schools to be free to resident children and provides that no sectarian instruction may be allowed in them.
religion_connection: Limits sectarian instruction in public district schools.
scope_note: The released-time authorization in the same section is normalized separately.
notes: Normalized from the verified Wisconsin baseline.

subject: released time for religious instruction
legal_effect: Authorizes the Legislature to permit release of public-school students during regular school hours for religious instruction outside the district school.
religion_connection: Creates an explicit constitutional authorization for religion-specific released time.
scope_note: Classification A describes the explicit religion-specific legal category, not historical causation.
notes: Normalized separately from the no-sectarian-instruction clause.

subject: released time for religious instruction
legal_effect: Permits students, with written parental permission and subject to statutory conditions, to be excused from school for religious instruction outside the school and establishes time, transportation, and responsibility rules.
religion_connection: Creates an explicit religion-specific school attendance accommodation.
scope_note: State ex rel. Holt v. Thompson addressed Wisconsin's released-time framework; broader case-law analysis remains an expansion item.
explanatory_authority: State ex rel. Holt v. Thompson, 66 Wis. 2d 659, 225 N.W.2d 678 (1975)
notes: Normalized from the verified Wisconsin baseline.

subject: religious observance and practice in employment
legal_effect: Treats specified failures to reasonably accommodate religious observance or practice as creed discrimination unless accommodation would impose undue hardship, subject to statutory exceptions involving religious organizations and religion-related employment.
religion_connection: Protects religious observance and practice against specified employment burdens and discrimination.
scope_note: Coverage and exceptions depend on the Wisconsin Fair Employment Act's definitions and terms.
notes: Normalized from the verified Wisconsin baseline.

subject: religious liberty, discrimination, officeholding, witnesses, and jurors
legal_effect: Protects free exercise and enjoyment of religious profession and worship without discrimination or preference and bars religious belief from making a person incompetent for office or service as a witness or juror, subject to the text's peace-and-safety limitation.
religion_connection: Limits religious discrimination and qualification while protecting religious exercise and civic participation.
scope_note: Historical motive is not assigned in the current profile.
notes: Normalized from the verified Wyoming baseline.

subject: state money for sectarian or religious societies and institutions
legal_effect: Provides that state money shall not be given or appropriated to a sectarian or religious society or institution.
religion_connection: Restricts state financial support for sectarian or religious organizations or institutions.
scope_note: The text remains in force, but application of state no-aid provisions is subject to controlling federal Free Exercise doctrine.
notes: Historical origins require separate research.

subject: religious control, tests, services, and sectarian instruction in education
legal_effect: Restricts public-school funds for institutions controlled by religious organizations and bars sectarian instruction, qualifications, or tests, required attendance at religious services, and state-school teaching or favoring of sectarian tenets or doctrines.
religion_connection: Limits sectarian control, public support, religious tests, compelled services, and sectarian instruction in state education.
scope_note: Funding applications are subject to controlling federal constitutional doctrine; this first-pass record groups related Article 7 provisions.
notes: Historical causation remains pending.

subject: Wyoming Religious Freedom Restoration Act
legal_effect: Provides that state action may not substantially burden religious exercise, including through a generally applicable rule, unless the government satisfies a compelling-interest and least-restrictive-means standard, with specified claims, defenses, and relief.
religion_connection: Protects religious exercise against specified state and local governmental burdens.
scope_note: The 2025 session law was enacted with earlier numbering; the current consolidated Wyoming Statutes place the Act in Chapter 29.
primary_authority: Wyoming Legislature, current Title 9, W.S. §§ 9-29-101 through 9-29-104 — https://www.wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title09.pdf
notes: Effective July 1, 2025; current codification controls.

formal_citation: Former Md. Ann. Code art. 27, § 521 (Sunday closing law at issue in McGowan v. Maryland)
subject: Sunday closing and retail sales
legal_effect: The former provision generally prohibited Sunday merchandise sales subject to statutory exceptions.
religion_connection: The U.S. Supreme Court's historical review stated that the original Sunday labor laws were motivated by religious forces, while concluding that the Maryland law's purpose and effect by 1961 had become a secular day of rest and recreation.
competing_causes: By 1961, the stated operative rationale emphasized uniform rest, recreation, and general welfare rather than religious observance.
scope_note: This is a historical-causation record for the former provision litigated in McGowan. It does not classify current Maryland Sunday-sales restrictions.
primary_authority: Former Md. Ann. Code art. 27, § 521, as described in McGowan v. Maryland, 366 U.S. 420 (1961) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/366/420
notes: Category B records documented religious origin. The same case is explicit that the law's then-current purpose was secular; origin and current rationale are separate fields.

subject: K–12 tuition assistance and school choice
legal_effect: Provides state-funded Choice Scholarships to eligible Indiana K–12 students to offset tuition at participating schools that satisfy program requirements.
religion_connection: Religiously affiliated schools may participate and the program was challenged under Indiana's religion clauses, but eligibility is not limited to religious schools. The Indiana Supreme Court described the direct benefit as expanded educational options for families and identified that as a valid secular purpose.
competing_causes: Religious-school participation created church-state litigation, but religion is not the program's eligibility basis or stated educational purpose.
scope_note: Category E describes the documented program purpose; it does not imply that religious organizations played no role in school-choice advocacy.
primary_authority: Indiana Department of Education, Choice Scholarship Program (authorized under IC 20-51-1 and IC 20-51-4) — https://www.in.gov/doe/students/indiana-choice-scholarship-program/
notes: Current IDOE materials describe the program as expanding access to educational opportunities; Meredith held religious-school benefits ancillary to family educational choice.
